title: Cross-mode admission controller for constraint-normalized canary sequencing and shadow traffic
creator: Aisha Ramanujan
description:
Background: Teams deploy the same model release to hosted, dedicated, and private footprints but current rollout primitives assume homogeneous constraints. That leads to unsafe promotions (e.g., promoting a model that passes hosted evals but fails on Dedicated due to quantization kernel mismatch or on Private due to KMS policy/egress rules).

Problem: We need an admission controller / sequencer that normalizes environment-specific constraints, sequences canary exposures (A/B + shadow), and performs automated rollback when cross-mode invariants are violated — without requiring teams to hand-craft three separate rollout configs.

Goals: Provide a single deployment manifest that: 1) compiles environment capability hints into per-mode exposure plans; 2) orchestrates staged canaries + shadow traffic across modes with time/metric gates; 3) supports automatic rollback and selective re-route to compatible model variants; 4) emits deterministic audits for compliance and SRE playbooks.

Non-goals: Replacing runtime kernel selection internals (serving runtime handles kernels), full model validation (we rely on per-mode validation hooks), or replacing tenant-level schema for model manifests.

Proposal summary: Implement a Cross-Mode Admission Controller (CMAC) service that: - Accepts a canonical rollout manifest (single source of truth). - Resolves environment constraint profiles (hosted, dedicated, private) and synthesizes per-mode rollout plans. - Performs simulated admissions (preflight) against capacity/capability matrix and flags incompatibilities. - Drives a sequencer that:  * stages canary percentages per-mode (time-based + metric gates)  * mirrors shadow traffic to non-primary modes for regression detection  * switches routing to fallback model variants when SLO regressions exceed thresholds  * triggers automatic rollback and creates a safe mitigation (traffic fencing + fallback routing)

High-level flow: 1) User submits release manifest referencing model version(s) and a policy block for canary/ab/shadow preferences. 2) CMAC queries environment profiles (capacity, KMS availability, quantization support, kernel compatibility tags) and tenant policies. 3) CMAC synthesizes an execution plan and runs a preflight simulation (synthetic traffic templates) to detect regressions or capacity violations. 4) If preflight passes, CMAC kicks off staged exposures; it monitors per-route telemetry and applies metric gates defined by the release policy. 5) On gate failure, CMAC executes rollback playbook: immediate holdback of new variant, route to last-known-good, create incident artifacts, and optionally escalate to manual rollback if automated steps didn't restore SLOs within timeout.

Trade-offs and rationale: - Centralizing admission logic avoids duplication but increases blast radius for bugs; mitigate via strong test harness and feature flags. - Synthesis may be conservative for private deployments (limit canary size) to avoid regulatory/data residency issues. - Auto-rollback uses conservative thresholds by default; teams can opt-in to faster/softer policies.

Implementation outline (high-level tasks):
- API: rollout manifest schema extension + validation.
- Capability store: per-environment capability profiles and discovery hooks.
- Planner: constraint resolver and per-mode sequencing engine.
- Sequencer: state machine that enforces gates, schedules exposures, and submits routing changes.
- Safety: simulation harness, canary canary (self-test), and replay-mode for debugging.
- Telemetry: per-model/tenant SLO time-series, rollout events stream for Console and audit logs.
- Integrations: Runtime router (traffic ops), Console (UI + timeline), KMS policy checks, and Dedicated capacity API.

Deliverables: API schema draft, CMAC service prototype, integration adapters for runtime and Console, unit+integration test suites, rollout runbook for SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical manifest accepts new 'mode_constraints' and 'sequencing_policy' fields and returns schema validation errors for invalid configs
CMAC can synthesize per-mode plans given three distinct environment profiles and expose a dry-run plan with identified incompatibilities
Sequencer can run a staged canary across hosted and dedicated with independent percentage ramps and enforce a latency/error gate that pauses promotion when thresholds exceeded
Shadow traffic mirroring can be enabled per-mode and instrumented so that console shows shadow vs primary deltas for chosen metrics

Auto-rollback triggers when any environment's p95 latency or error rate breaches configured gate for longer than the configured grace window, and rollback restores previous routing within the SLO target
All rollout events and decision traces are persisted to audit logs with tenant, release, and decision reason
End-to-end tests simulate a quantization-incompatibility that causes dedicated preflight failure and CMAC surfaces a clear remediation hint (use alternative quantized variant)
test_plan: Unit tests for constraint resolver covering KMS/egress/kernel/quantization flags
Integration test: dry-run synthesis for a manifest across the three environments with mocked capability store
Canary failure simulation: inject latency regressions and assert sequencer pauses and rollback executes
Shadow delta reporting test: replay historical traffic and validate metric diff pipeline
Chaos test: simulate network partition to private control plane and validate graceful fallback to hosted-only routing where policy permits
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dogfood in staging with one tenant (staging account) — dry-run and simulated canary (no real traffic)
Stage 1: opt-in beta for 3 pilot tenants across Hosted and Dedicated — monitoring dashboards + SRE on-call
Stage 2: broader controlled rollout (10% of release teams) with feature flag gating and rollback safe mode
Stage 3: GA after 3 successful rolling windows and security review sign-off
telemetry_and_observability: Per-rollout timeline view in Console with per-environment metric overlays (latency, errors, token cost)
Audit trail events stream that includes decision reasons and preflight simulation outputs
Alert: rollout-paused and rollback-executed that create incidents with links to affected tenants and run logs
Synthetic traffic guard: per-manifest synthetic templates that can be replayed for repro and debugging
